transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I know it probably sounds a little silly, so I'm sorry if it's not a big deal. But I just... I keep getting really stuck on this one little thing about my face. 

There's this tiny, um, uneven spot right around my nose and my cheek. I notice it a lot in photos, and especially under the bright fluorescent lights at the store where I work. I've asked a few people about it and they always say they don't even see it, which I guess is good? But... I don't know, it just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you find yourself thinking about this uneven spot on your face at times when you're not looking in a mirror or seeing photos of yourself?

Um... I don't think so? Or, well, I try really hard not to. I definitely don't want to sound like I'm completely obsessed with myself or anything. 

If I'm just at home watching a movie or doing chores, it's not really on my mind at all. It mostly just pops up if I'm at the register and a customer is kind of staring at me, because then I start wondering if they're looking at the spot. But I definitely don't just sit around thinking about it all day when there aren't any mirrors around. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm, like, crazy or totally vain for bringing it up. Is it normal to just wonder about it when people look at you?
Has worrying about the uneven spot on your face ever caused you to avoid social situations or interactions with others?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I avoid people. I mean, I still go to work every day and do my job, and I see my friends sometimes. I'm definitely not a hermit or anything like that! 

Sometimes, if I'm having a really bad day with it, I might... I don't know, maybe I'll offer to organize the stock room instead of being on the main register, just so I'm not right under those bright lights with everyone looking at me. But I still talk to people! And if my friends want to go out, I'll go. I might just try to sit in a booth where the lighting is a little softer, or maybe I'll pass on being in a bunch of selfies. 

But I'm definitely still social and doing things. That's pretty normal, right? To just want to feel comfortable when you're out?
Do you ever find yourself repeatedly checking your face in mirrors or reflections throughout the day?

Um... I guess I do check it sometimes? But not, like, an abnormal amount, I promise! I just... well, on my breaks at work, I might run to the bathroom and just take a quick peek in the mirror. You know, just to make sure everything looks okay? 

But sometimes I guess I do get a little caught up trying to fix my hair so it kind of falls over that side of my face. And... I hate to admit this, because it sounds so silly and shallow, but I do kind of look at the girls who come through my line and think about how smooth their skin is compared to mine. 

I've actually... well, a couple of times I've taken a little too long in the bathroom trying to get my hair just right, and I ended up being a minute or two late getting back to the register. My manager didn't yell at me or anything, but I felt really bad about it. 

That's just normal insecurity stuff, right? Everyone checks the mirror a few times a day, don't they? I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform specific routines or behaviors to try to cope with your concerns about the uneven spot on your face?

Um... routines? No, I wouldn't say I have any routines. That sounds so intense, you know? Like I'm totally fixated on it, and I'm really not. 

I just... I mean, I have a normal morning routine, like everyone else. I wash my face, put on a little makeup, maybe try to blend a little extra concealer over that spot if it looks particularly bad that day. But that's just basic grooming, isn't it? I don't do anything weird or specific just to deal with it. 

I really just try to go about my day like a normal person. You don't think washing your face and putting on makeup counts as a weird routine, do you? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Has your concern about the uneven spot on your face ever interfered with your ability to do your job effectively or enjoy your time with friends?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it really interferes! I mean, I still have a lot of fun with my friends, I promise. We always have a good time when we go out. 

But as for work... um... I guess maybe just a tiny bit? I really hate to even admit this to you, because I always try to be such a hard worker, you know? But... well, my manager did actually say something to me recently. He noticed that I've been coming back from my breaks a few minutes late—like I mentioned before with the mirror—and he said I've been moving a little slower at the register lately. I think I just get distracted worrying about how the overhead lights are hitting my face, and I lose my focus for a second. 

It's just really embarrassing because I'm actually trying to get promoted right now, and I'm so worried that this is making me look unreliable to him. I really don't want him to think I'm a bad employee! I'm trying so hard to do a good job. Getting a little distracted sometimes doesn't mean I'm failing at my job, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.
Do you feel like you have to check your face in the mirror when you're getting ready for work or going out with friends?

Um... well, when I'm getting ready, I guess I do look in the mirror, but just the normal amount, I think? Like, just to make sure I look presentable before I leave the house. I promise I don't just stand there staring for hours or anything! 

But, um... like I was saying before about being at work... I do kind of end up checking my face in the bathroom mirror on my breaks. And... well, I guess I spend a little time trying to fix my hair so it falls around that spot just right. And then when I'm back at the register, I do catch myself comparing my skin to the girls who come through my line. It's just so hard not to notice when their skin looks so perfect, you know? 

And... yeah, sometimes I do take a little too long in the bathroom fixing my hair, and that's why I've been a few minutes late getting back to the register. I really hate that I do that, and I'm trying so hard to be better about it. I just want to look nice for work, you know? That makes sense, doesn't it? I really hope you don't think I'm just being vain.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you think about the uneven spot on your face?

Um... anxious? No, I wouldn't say I get really anxious or upset about it. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting around crying over it or having panic attacks or anything like that. I promise I'm keeping it together!

I guess sometimes it just... bothers me a little bit? Like, maybe I feel a tiny bit self-conscious when I think about it too much, especially if I'm under those bright store lights. But it's just a normal amount of being self-conscious, you know? Like how anyone would feel if they had a spot they didn't like. 

I really try to stay positive and not let it get to me. Everyone has little things they wish they could change about themselves, right? I just want to make sure I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than it really is. It's totally normal to feel a little bummed out about a bad skin day sometimes, isn't it?
Do you feel like you have to fix your hair in a specific way to cover the uneven spot on your face?

Oh, um, yeah... I guess I did mention that a little bit earlier, didn't I? I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right! 

But yes, when I go to the bathroom on my breaks, I do end up looking in the mirror and trying to fix my hair so it falls around that spot. I just try to brush pieces forward so it kind of... shadows it, I guess? I really just want to look neat and presentable for the customers, I promise I'm not trying to be obsessive about it. But sometimes I just can't get it to lay right, and I take so long messing with it that I end up being late getting back to the register. 

And then, I don't know, once I'm back out there, I just catch myself comparing my face to the girls who come through my line. It's so silly of me, and I know I shouldn't do it, but they just look so flawless. I'm really trying to be better about not taking so long in the bathroom, though! It's pretty normal to want to style your hair to flatter your face, right? I'm not doing anything too weird, am I?
Do you feel like you have to fix your hair in a specific way to cover the uneven spot on your face every time you see yourself in a mirror?

Oh! Um... no, definitely not *every* single time. I promise I don't just stop and stare at every mirror I pass! I really don't want you to think I'm completely obsessed or anything. 

But, um... I guess, like I was just saying, it really happens the most on my breaks at work. I go into the bathroom and end up checking my face, and... yeah, I do fix my hair around it to try and hide it. And then I get caught up comparing myself to the girls who come through my line, and... well, that's how I end up taking so long that I'm late getting back to the register. 

I know I keep bringing the work thing up, I'm sorry if I sound like a broken record! I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you. It's totally normal to want to touch up your hair in the bathroom during a shift, right? I'm doing okay answering these?

Um... I think it's mostly just wanting to look nice? I really don't feel like I *have* to do it, like I'm not out of control or anything. I just want to look my best, you know? 

Like I said before—and I'm so sorry to keep talking about the same thing, I hope I'm not being annoying!—it's just when I'm on my breaks. I guess I just want to feel a little more confident before I go back out there, especially since I find myself comparing my face to all those pretty girls who come through my line. 

I know I said I sometimes take a little too long and end up late getting back to the register... but I really am trying to stop doing that! I promise I'm working on it. It's just normal wanting to look presentable for work, right? I'm not doing anything wrong, am I?

Oh, gosh, no! Not like a disaster or anything. I promise I don't think anything crazy is going to happen. I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record, and I'm really sorry to keep bringing up the exact same situation... I really hope I'm giving you what you need!

Because I know I'll be comparing myself to all the girls who come through my line, and I just want to feel okay before I have to ring them up. That's really the only reason I end up taking so long and sometimes get back to my register late. I just want to look nice for the customers so I don't feel bad standing next to them. That makes sense, right? I'm answering okay?
Do you feel like fixing your hair to cover the uneven spot is something you need to do, or is it just something you want to do?

Um, I guess it's... it's just something I want to do? I really don't want you to think it's this big, uncontrollable need or anything. I just like to look nice! 

I know I've said this a million times—and I'm so, so sorry for repeating myself again, I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer!—but it really just comes down to my breaks. I go into the bathroom, check the mirror, and just kind of arrange my hair so I feel a little better about that spot. Because, you know, I see all those really pretty girls coming through my line, and I just start comparing myself to them. 

And I know I mentioned that sometimes I get caught up doing that and end up a little late getting back to my register... but I'm really trying to be better about watching the clock! I just want to feel okay before I go back out there. It's totally normal to want to feel confident at work, isn't it? Am I making sense?
Do you feel like you would be able to stop fixing your hair to cover the uneven spot if you wanted to?

Um, yes! I mean, I'm pretty sure I could stop if I really tried. It's not like an addiction or anything. I just... well, I guess I just haven't tried to stop yet? 

I know I keep bringing up the same stuff, and I really hope I'm not boring you or making you think I'm completely obsessed. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right! But yeah, it's just that thing on my breaks, where I go to the bathroom and look in the mirror and fix my hair to sort of hide that spot. Especially because I see all those gorgeous girls coming through my line, and I just can't help but compare myself to them, you know? 

And, um, I know I said I sometimes lose track of time and get back to the register a little late because of it... which I know isn't good, and I really am trying to stop doing that part! But as for fixing my hair, I could totally stop if I needed to. I just like feeling a little more put together. That's okay to say, right? I'm not sounding too crazy?
Do you feel like fixing your hair to cover the uneven spot is something that you do because you feel like you have to, or because it's just what you prefer to do?

Oh, definitely just a preference! I don't feel like I *have* to do it, I promise. It's really just a choice. 

I feel so silly, I know I'm basically telling you the exact same story again. I'm really, really sorry, I hope I'm not frustrating you! I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're asking for.
